evidence.note: Opens with an explicit 8-item numbered subsystem plan (start.sh, skeleton, SigV4, storage, S3, admin, console, audit), establishing a concrete done-vs-remaining scaffold.

Systematic verification sweep walks the subsystem list and marks items off one by one (basic S3, multipart, presigned, console, cross-tenant, versioning, lifecycle, audit filtering, stats, special chars, concurrency, policy) — a maintained coverage picture.
Detected presigned 403, diagnosed the cause (boto3 SigV2 vs forced v4) in a single pass and fixed it — recognized the impasse rather than looping/thrashing on the signature mismatch.
Says 'let me look at notification' then pivots to a smoke check; bucket-notification delivery/retry is never actually verified — a required subsystem silently dropped at the horizon.
Final re-review enumerates specific residual contract items to check (console route, static paths, quotas, audit rid, session revocation), showing granular but incomplete contract tracking.

reasoning: The agent maintained a usable, mostly granular checklist of subsystems and marked them off through a dedicated verification sweep (anchor 5), and it recognized the presigned-signature impasse quickly without thrashing, naming the cause (leaning toward anchor 8). However, fine-grained contract coverage slipped: notifications were mentioned then never verified, and the error-code/testid matrix was not systematically reconciled to completion — leaving a required area silently dropped at the horizon. This places it between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 6.
